title: Shoup reports from Betio
pull: Day two on Betio, from the man in charge
quote: Casualties many; percentage dead not known; combat efficiency: We are winning.
quoteBy: Col. David M. Shoup, situation report from Betio, 21 November 1943

facts.text: Late on the afternoon of 21 November 1943, the second day on Betio, Col. David M. Shoup sent a situation report to Maj. Gen. Julian C. Smith, commander of the 2nd Marine Division. It described the lines at 4 p.m. and was received by the division at 5:06 p.m.
The report ended: "Casualties many; percentage dead not known; combat efficiency: We are winning." It became one of the most famous messages in Marine Corps history.

Shoup, 38, was the junior colonel in the division. He had helped plan the landing, and when the colonel of the 2nd Marines fell ill just before the battle, General Smith promoted Shoup and gave him command of the assault.
On D Day his amtrac was hit and he was wounded in the leg by a shell fragment. Standing waist deep in water beside the long pier, he worked his radio to get units ashore.

By mid afternoon on the second day the tide had turned. Marines had pushed across the airfield to the south shore, ammunition and water were coming in, and fresh battalions of the 6th Marines were landing.
"I thought up until 1300 today it was touch and go," said Lt. Col. Presley M. Rixey, Shoup's artillery commander. "Then I knew we would win."
Organized resistance on Betio ended at 1:05 p.m. on 23 November.
Shoup received the Medal of Honor, the only one of the four Marines awarded it for Tarawa who lived to receive it. His citation says he fought on "despite innumerable obstacles and heavy casualties."
In 1959 President Dwight D. Eisenhower chose him as the 22nd Commandant of the Marine Corps.

photoNote: Marines take cover among logs and rubble behind the seawall on Red Beach 3, Betio, a Marine at right with an ammunition belt, palms stripped bare against a dark sky. National Archives 127-GR-119-64002 (NAID 532385), USMC photo, use Unrestricted, public domain. Exact day not given (taken during the battle, 20 to 23 Nov 1943). 1920 x 1490 grayscale from the 3000 px TIFF, NARA number at bottom edge cropped off. Works well dimmed under the quote; the right half is brightest. No Shoup on Betio photo could be fetched (Wikimedia rate limited); the famous one of Shoup at his command post beside a Japanese bunker is on Commons and could replace this if wanted.
photoCredit: Marines take cover behind the seawall on Red Beach 3, Betio, Tarawa, November 1943. National Archives 127-GR-119-64002, public domain.

declassified.fact: Shoup kept a combat notebook at Tarawa. In it he wrote: "I realize that I am but a bit of chaff from the threshings of life blown into the pages of history by the unknown winds of chance."
